title: CR functions at CR singularities: approximation, extension, and hulls

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation numbering gap between equations (5) and (7)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper jumps from equation (5) in Example 3.9 to equation (7) in Example 3.11, with no equation (6) present in the text. Equation (6) likely belongs to one of the missing Sections 4-9. This does not affect mathematical correctness but is a minor presentation inconsistency that could confuse readers.

Equation (9) writes DH(X) with the second union component having Im z₂ ≤ 0, whereas from the attachment to X₂ (which requires Im z₂ < 0), the strict inequality should be Im z₂ < 0. The boundary Im z₂ = 0 is in the closure of DH(X) but not necessarily in DH(X) itself. This is a minor precision issue in set notation.

summary:
Verification of 'CR functions at CR singularities: approximation, extension, and hulls' by Lebl, Noell, and Ravisankar found no critical mathematical errors. The paper provides clear, rigorous definitions of three classes of CR functions (CR, CR_P, CR_H) and develops the theory of disc hulls (DH, SADH, iterated SADH) for studying extension and approximation at CR singular points. All 11 equations were verified as mathematically correct. The 16 formal statements (theorems, lemmas, definitions, proofs) were found logically consistent. Citations are to well-established works in CR geometry (Baouendi-Trèves, Severi, Lewy, Kohn-Rossi, Mergelyan, etc.) with no evidence of fabrication or misattribution. Cross-section consistency analysis confirmed internal coherence of Sections 1-3.

Four low-confidence warnings were noted: (1) a gap in equation numbering between equations (5) and (7), (2) a minor imprecision in equation (9) regarding boundary inclusion (≤ vs <), (3) the proof of Lemma 2.4 for the simply connected case is very terse, and (4) the paper is truncated — Sections 4-9, containing the main constructive results promised in the abstract, are not included in the provided file. None of these rise to the level of requiring correction under lenient strictness.

The mathematical content present is rigorous, well-organized, and contributes meaningfully to the understanding of CR functions near singularities. The examples (3.9-3.14) are particularly well-constructed and effectively illustrate the subtleties of disc hull behavior.
